cases.reason: Named registered-style earn-and-learn electrician apprenticeship with a concrete public application route and disclosed fees. Paid work begins on assignment to a contractor, so the four-year length is program duration after entry, not delay before pay. Competitive selection and cost are preserved as caveats rather than grounds for exclusion.
criticalDetails: Four-year program combining paid work for a participating contractor with classroom training; apprentices are assigned to a contractor upon selection.
Published charges: $40 nonrefundable application fee plus $187 monthly during training; resource text says to confirm current costs.
Applying does not guarantee selection; admission is competitive.
Must be 18 by program start and meet education and algebra requirements, or an approved alternative; identification and school records required.
Documented military service or electrical experience may qualify for requirement exceptions.
Must be able to reach regional work sites; training centers are in Phoenix and job sites vary across the program area, so travel from Mesa applies to both classroom and assignments.
Physical demands include ladders, confined spaces and regular 50-pound lifting; program should be asked about essential job requirements and accommodations.
Classes accompany full-time work.
Apply via How to Apply at https://pejatc.org/how-to-apply/; webservices@pejatc.org for application help or to arrange use of a training-center computer.
Check the current application deadline before paying the fee.

cases.reason: Named public program (DES-administered SCSEP) that pays participants while training, with published eligibility and multiple DES-listed grantee phone numbers covering Maricopa County including Mesa. Paid help begins at placement with a host agency, though slot availability is uncertain.
criticalDetails: Part-time paid community-service training, typically averaging about 20 hours weekly, paid at the highest applicable minimum wage.

Eligibility: Arizona resident, 55 or older, unemployed, authorized to work, income at or below 125% of the federal poverty level, and facing a job barrier (examples given: limited English, disability, poor job prospects).
Arizona Job Connection registration is required; staff verify eligibility.
DES-listed contacts for Maricopa County: 602-841-0403 (AARP/Easterseals route), AARP 928-395-2261, NICOA 505-292-2001.
Temporary training with limited places and possible waiting lists.
Wages may affect other benefits; participation time limits apply and should be asked about before enrolling.
Host-agency training site is arranged by the office, so the travel destination is not known until placement.
Program page: https://des.az.gov/services/older-adults/senior-community-service-employment-program

cases.reason: Local staffing office physically in Mesa with a verified address, phone, email and posted hours, free placement to the job seeker, and a durable public intake route rather than a single stale opening. Temp, evaluation-hire and direct-hire pathways give a realistic short path to paid work.
criticalDetails: No job placement fee to the job seeker; weekly pay.
849 N. Dobson Rd., Suite 107, Mesa, AZ 85201; Monday–Thursday 8 AM–5 PM, Friday 8 AM–3 PM.
Phone 480-820-3700; email jobs.mesaaz@expresspros.com; call before visiting to arrange application help by phone or in person.
One application connects to several employers; roles include warehouse and manufacturing, skilled trades, office and customer service, and professional positions.
If applying online, the application must be submitted to the Mesa office; saving an account alone does not send it.
Requirements vary by job (experience, skills, schedule, licensure); some positions require a skills assessment.
Placement depends on a suitable opening; applying does not guarantee a job.

Some benefits (health-plan options, dental, vision, life and disability, retirement, confidential counseling) require minimum hours or weeks worked; ExpressLearn courses are only for workers already employed by Express.
Bring work-eligibility documents to an interview; have work and education history, references and contact details ready.
Ask about pay, schedule, work location, transportation and any required equipment or testing costs before accepting an assignment.
After an assignment ends, contact the office to be considered for another.

cases.reason: Named disability supported-employment provider with Mesa sites, a working phone number and a stated referral address. Guidance directs that an actionable named referral not be discarded solely because a referral is required; the funding and wage questions are preserved rather than treated as disqualifying.
criticalDetails: Services include career planning, work preparation, computer skills, job development, supported employment, community work experience and ongoing support.
Serves people with disabilities; entry and funding depend on program and referral, with VR, DDD, behavioral-health plans and private pay listed.
Call 480-969-3800 and ask for Employment Related Services; referrals are sent to referrals@copahealth.org.
People with a case manager, DDD support coordinator or VR counselor should ask that person about a referral.
Employment services are listed at two Mesa sites plus other Valley locations; main office 924 N. Country Club Dr., Mesa — call for the correct employment site before traveling.
Transportation is offered to community group work sites, but not necessarily to intake or training; ask separately.
Facility training, group work experience and competitive job support are different services with different implications.
The provider page describes what businesses pay Copa, which does not establish a participant's wage.
Program page: https://copahealth.org/copa-employment-related-services/

cases.reason: Free, named nine-week occupational training with published class schedule, application phone, fax and online route, aimed specifically at adults facing employment barriers. Retained despite the Phoenix location and heavy screening; travel burden and screening rules are preserved as consequential details.
criticalDetails: Two tracks: Community Kitchen (culinary) and LIFT (logistics, inventory, forklift). Training is free.
Nine weeks, Monday–Friday, 7 AM–3 PM at 3003 W. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85017 — a long daily commute from Mesa with a 7 AM start.
Eligibility: 18+, authorized to work, facing employment barriers, ready for steady work, able to attend consistently.
Background and drug screening apply, including random drug tests during training; arson and registered-sex-offender exclusions are published.
Living arrangement requirement: shelter, own or rented home, or halfway house; other arrangements should be raised with staff.
Apply by calling 602-343-3183, applying online, dropping off an application, or faxing to 480-780-3799; staff arrange an interview and notify of acceptance, waitlist or decline.
Housing is not included and employment is not guaranteed.
Program page: https://www.firstfoodbank.org/learn/programs/community-kitchen/

cases.reason: The paid work component (Neighborhood Brigade) is restricted to residents of specified SVdP housing programs, so it is not a stand-alone public job route. criticalDetails: Neighborhood Brigade paid cleanup work is limited to residents of Ozanam Manor and the Washington Street housing program.
Rosalie's Place is workforce housing for adults working or looking for work, with employment and money-management support; staff screen applicants.
Conflicting published cost terms: the Rosalie's workforce page describes free housing with residents saving 60% of net income, while the general intake page states residents with income pay 30%.
Housing screening 602-850-6900, 8 AM–3 PM: phone screening followed by an in-person interview. Rosalie's Place questions 602-261-6870, Monday–Friday 8 AM–3 PM.
Washington Street shelter requires a partner referral and does not accept walk-ups.
Rosalie's Place and Ozanam Manor: 320 W. Watkins Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85003; Washington Street shelter: 2739 E. Washington St., Phoenix, AZ 85034 — all in Phoenix, not Mesa.
Mesa Dining Room, 49 W. Broadway Rd., 602-619-9411, is listed among work-readiness locations, but the actual local service and schedule are unconfirmed.
Beds and paid crew openings are limited.
